audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[N].side read 'Yasuo' while content win[0..6] read 'Brand', the packet levelChart reads Brand on all seven rows, every phases[N].why describes Brand winning that stage, and the matchup is 52.07% over 726 games.
audit.why: The side column is the lone outlier against five agreeing sources. This is exactly the row-argues-with-its-own-sentence defect.
audit.corrected: Flipped all seven sides to Brand as one atomic group and rewrote every why to be Yasuo-specific. win[0..6] already hold 'Brand', so the pairs agree without a content-layer edit.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d claimed a 'fifteen-second' Wind Wall window.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17 — fifteen seconds is not a rank. Last Breath is 70/50/30 and needs an airborne target he cannot create alone reliably in lane.
audit.corrected: Real numbers now in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0..2], phases[6].why and spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4], spikes[1].text and mid all claimed Pyroclasm's 'multi-angle bounce' beats Wind Wall.
audit.why: Brand's own kit flags Q, W and R as projectiles blockable by Wind Wall-class effects. Only Conflagration (E) is unblockable. Telling a player their ult goes through the wall is a fabricated interaction that loses the fight.
audit.corrected: Rewrote all three around the real rule: E is the wall-proof spell, and the R goes out in the window after the wall expires. Also added the Way of the Wanderer shield (missingInteractions shield-absorbs-burst) to dontsFull[2].d.

audit.why: Wind Wall's 25s-to-17s cooldown and 4s duration is the entire timing structure of this lane.
audit.corrected: Now carries Wind Wall 25s/17s/4s, Conflagration 13s, Sweeping Blade 0.5s recharge.

audit.whatIsWrong: early said 'Wind Wall can only block one cast at a time'.
audit.why: Riot's text: it blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds — a duration, not a charge.
audit.corrected: Restated as 4 seconds of coverage on a 25s cooldown.

edits.before: W-poke his last-hits from max range — the pillar chunks early and the lane learns to flinch by level 2.
edits.after: Pillar of Flame at 900 range punishes a 475-range melee who must walk up for Steel Tempest last-hits.

edits.before: E joins: the point-and-click ablaze into Q-stun threat is already a kill pattern with jungle help.
edits.after: E joins and it is the one spell Wind Wall cannot block — ablaze, then Sear stuns his walk-up.

edits.before: Full kit: E-Q stun into W is half a health bar at level 3. He respects every cast from here or pays.
edits.after: Full kit at 3: E-Q-W chunks him, and Wind Wall on 25s covers only one of your three casts.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — rotation poke on every wave contact. Blaze stacks make even chip trades unfair.
edits.after: Lost Chapter timing: his Sweeping Blade needs a target, so clear the wave and he cannot reach you.

edits.before: Pyroclasm online — any clumped trade is now a detonation chain. Lane all-ins favor the arsonist.
edits.after: Last Breath needs a knock-up; alone in lane he has none, so your R still decides the all-in.

edits.before: Liandry's spike: the burn makes every rotation percent-health math. Force extended exchanges.
edits.after: Liandry's spike: the burn keeps ticking after his Way of the Wanderer shield is spent.

edits.before: Late Brand is a teamfight detonator: spread Blaze, R the clump, and watch three health bars argue with physics.
edits.after: Late, Wind Wall is 17s maxed and lasts 4 seconds — spread Blaze with E, then R the clump when it drops.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E-Q stun package like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Wind Wall (W): 25s at rank 1, 17s maxed, 4 seconds of cover — it eats Sear, Pillar of Flame and Pyroclasm alike, so bait it and count. - Conflagration (E) on 13s is the only spell it cannot block. - Sweeping Blade recharges every 0.5s.

edits.before: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Conflagration is not a projectile — it lands through Wind Wall and sets the ablaze that Sear needs.

edits.before: E the instant ablaze, Q the stun, W the stunned body, walk — the full package chunks half a bar and the burn writes the receipt.
edits.after: Sweeping Blade needs a target to dash to — drop the pillar on the minion he is heading for and the delay lands as he arrives.

edits.before: Yasuo burns Wind Wall on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Two Steel Tempest stacks means the third is a knock-up — stun before it.

edits.before: That is Yasuo’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Pillar of Flame alone leaves Sear unbanked, and his dash costs him nothing.

edits.before: Your stun only exists on ablaze targets — a Q thrown at a clean health bar is the most expensive miss in your kit.
edits.after: Inside 475 he chains Sweeping Blade off every minion in the wave while you stand still with E on a 13s cooldown.

edits.before: W-poking on cooldown with Q unbanked while his engage is loaded — Brand without the stun threat is a bonfire waiting for company.
edits.after: Way of the Wanderer builds a shield while he moves — it eats the front of your burst, so make him spend it before Sear goes out.

edits.before: Track Yasuo’s Wind Wall: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Wind Wall: 4 seconds that block Sear, Pillar of Flame and Pyroclasm alike. Conflagration is the one spell that goes through.

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Yasuo wins by walling your projectiles, chaining Sweeping Blade in, and cashing a knock-up into Last Breath.

edits.before: Carry through AoE math — no burst mage damages three targets like Brand; your job is the spacing that lets the bounces vote.
edits.after: Carry by spacing outside 475 — every pillar and every bounce is free while he has no target to dash through.

edits.before: If Yasuo gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Wind Wall extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with W-E clears and stay relevant through stun-burn peel.
edits.after: If Yasuo gets a kill his crit arrives early — farm with W-E from 900, never step inside 475 with E down, and bank Sear purely to stun the dash that starts the all-in.

edits.before: Level 6: his Wind Wall can't fully answer your multi-angle Pyroclasm threat, so your spike stays stronger.
edits.after: Level 6: Last Breath needs an airborne target, so alone in lane he has no way to open on your Pyroclasm.

edits.before: Your Pyroclasm bounce is very hard for him to Wind Wall (W) away completely, since it can bounce from multiple angles and punishes his all-in timing.
edits.after: Wind Wall blocks Pyroclasm like your other projectiles, so hold the 100s R for the seconds after the wall expires and his all-in has no cover left.

edits.before: At level 6 you keep the edge: Pyroclasm's multi-angle bounce is hard to fully wall off, so your all-in threat remains live even against his Wind Wall. Through your first item power spike your burst combo still outpaces anything he can do without a coordinated knock-up assist, keeping trades in your favor.
edits.after: At level 6 the all-in is yours on a timer: Wind Wall lasts 4 seconds on a 25s cooldown at rank 1, so bait it with a pillar and the window after it belongs to you. Through your first item power spike your burst combo still outpaces anything he can do without a coordinated knock-up assist, keeping trades in your favor.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 already favor you since Yasuo has no way to poke back at range, and this only compounds by levels 3-5 — Pillar of Flame chunks him every time he approaches to farm with Steel Tempest, and Wind Wall can only block one cast at a time, so you can bait it out before committing your real combo.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 already favor you since Yasuo has no way to poke back at range, and this only compounds by levels 3-5 — Pillar of Flame chunks him every time he approaches to farm with Steel Tempest, and Wind Wall covers only 4 seconds on a 25s cooldown, so bait it out before committing your real combo.

edits.before: Poke him relentlessly with Q since he has no ranged answer to Pillar of Flame
edits.after: Poke with Pillar of Flame (W); Wind Wall eats Sear but cannot cover the wave

edits.before: Bait Wind Wall by faking a Pyroclasm angle, then bounce it from a different direction
edits.after: Bait Wind Wall with a Pillar of Flame, then commit in the 4 seconds after it fades
